entries.clue: A piss is said to satisfy a demand (7)

indicatorNotes.is said: tells you to hear the words, not read them

blocks.note: a piss is a pee, so the words become 'a pee's', which run together when spoken

annotation.surface: A crude boast that relieving yourself will answer an urgent call.
annotation.walkthrough: The trick is to swap the vulgar word for its politer synonym first: 'a piss is' becomes 'a pee's', and only then does it sound like the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: To appease is to give someone what they are demanding so they calm down.

entries.clue: Expert wittering on? Not b–— likely! (8)

indicatorNotes.Not b–—: says to remove a B from the word before

blocks.note: wittering on is BABBLE; with one B taken away it becomes BABLE

annotation.surface: Someone scoffs 'Not bloody likely!' at the idea of an expert droning on.
annotation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'Not b–— likely' read as the censored oath 'Not bloody likely', but the setter means it literally: 'not B', one B dropped from BABBLE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something probable is likely, as in 'the probable outcome'.

entries.clue: An honour to cut journalist's plant (5)

indicatorNotes.to cut: the honour cuts into the journalist, splitting ED around it

blocks.note: ED = editor, the crossword's usual journalist; it opens to take the honour
MBE = Member of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

annotation.surface: A journalist's pot plant is honoured, or an honour is used to pay off a reporter's mole.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a noun in the surface, but it is the verb: to embed something is to plant it firmly. An embedded reporter travels with an army, which makes the journalist apt.
annotation.definitionFit: To embed something is to plant it firmly in its surroundings.

entries.clue: KKK members want this drink with creamy fudge (9)

indicatorNotes.fudge: to fudge is to mess about with, so the letters of CREAMY are rearranged

annotation.surface: A mocking picture of Klansmen craving a sweet drink and creamy fudge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fudge' pretends to be a sweet to go with the creamy drink; it is the instruction to jumble CREAMY. The KKK, the Ku Klux Klan, want white supremacy.
annotation.definitionFit: The Ku Klux Klan campaigns for white supremacy, the domination of other races by white people.

entries.clue: School gets dirt on objectionable type (7)

blocks.note: SCH is the standard abbreviation for school

annotation.surface: A school digs up dirt on an unpleasant character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gets dirt on' reads as uncovering scandal, but nobody is investigated: the word for dirt just follows school's abbreviation. Schmuck is Yiddish slang, common in American English.
annotation.definitionFit: A schmuck, from Yiddish, is a contemptible or foolish person.

entries.clue: (& 21ac.) Still a glow from this pathetic erection, however restrained? (5)

annotation.definition: Still a glow from this pathetic erection, however restrained?

blocks.note: the surface suggests lingering arousal; the setter means a smouldering stub that is still lit
a cigar is the stock phallic joke; a short, stubby, spent one is its pathetic end

annotation.surface: A smutty picture of a sad, half-hearted erection that still has a little glow in it.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a cigar butt: the stubby, burnt-down end of a phallic cigar that may still be glowing. The answer runs on into 21 across.
annotation.definitionFit: A cigar butt is the short leftover end of a smoked cigar, which can still be smouldering.

entries.clue: For now beastly husband's caught in trickery (9)

indicatorNotes.caught in: the husband is caught inside the word for trickery

blocks.note: wile = cunning trickery; it opens after W
H = husband, as in genealogy tables

annotation.surface: A husband has been caught playing nasty tricks, for the time being.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Husband's' is 'husband has', not possessive. The surface sounds like an affair being covered up for the time being.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'for now' and 'meanwhile' both mean in the time before something else happens.

entries.clue: Who'd be advised by lawyer to take a different line in court? (6)

indicatorNotes.take: CT takes the jumbled line inside it
indicatorNotes.a different: a different version of LINE, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court; it opens to take LIEN

annotation.surface: A lawyer advises someone to change their story in the witness box.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a lawyer telling someone to switch their testimony, and that someone is the client.
annotation.definitionFit: A client is the person a lawyer represents and advises.

entries.clue: Lice virtually spread by China – disaster that's barely covered by most campaigning politicians (7,6)

annotation.definition: that's barely covered by most campaigning politicians
annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for the thing it describes: something that's barely covered

indicatorNotes.virtually: almost all of the word, so LICE loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.spread: the letters are spread about, so rearranged

blocks.note: LICE without its last letter is LIC, then rearranged

annotation.surface: A pandemic-style scare about lice spreading from China, which politicians on the stump barely mention.
annotation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, fitting a disease story; it is Cockney rhyming slang, where 'china plate' means mate. The setter's jab is that the climate crisis gets little airtime on the campaign trail.
annotation.definitionFit: The climate crisis is the subject most campaigning politicians say little about.

entries.clue: Labour's focus: women – unruly mob (4)

indicatorNotes.unruly: an unruly mob is out of order, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: W = women, as on clothing sizes and toilet doors

annotation.surface: A political slogan: the Labour Party is concentrating on women voters and a rowdy crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party; here it is childbirth, and the womb is where it happens.
annotation.definitionFit: Labour in childbirth is centred on the womb, whose contractions push the baby out.

entries.clue: Slimy Matter, Act I – sadly unemotional (10)

indicatorNotes.sadly: things gone sadly wrong are out of order, so ACT I is rearranged

annotation.surface: A review of a play called 'Slimy Matter' whose first act left the audience cold.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make 'Slimy Matter, Act I' look like a play title; in crosswords capitals can be ignored, so it is just phlegm plus ACT I.
annotation.definitionFit: Phlegmatic means calm and unemotional; phlegm was once the humour thought to cause it.

entries.clue: D-dear Mary screwed outside refuse tip – romantic! (10)

indicatorNotes.screwed: screwed up, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.outside: the jumbled letters go around the E
indicatorNotes.tip: the tip of refuse is its end letter

blocks.note: the stammer gives an extra D; these nine letters are rearranged around the E

annotation.surface: Someone stammers 'D-dear Mary' after messing things up outside the rubbish dump, hardly a romantic setting.
annotation.walkthrough: The stammer is not decoration: 'D-dear' supplies two Ds. 'Tip' looks like a rubbish tip, a British word for a dump; here it is the tip, the end, of 'refuse'.
annotation.definitionFit: A romantic, as a noun, is an idealistic dreamer, a daydreamer.

entries.clue: Cause of fart's success on date (4)

annotation.surface: A bawdy explanation of why a date went well, or badly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fart's' is 'fart has': the definition stops at 'fart', and WIN sits on D.
annotation.definitionFit: Wind, trapped gas, is what makes someone fart.

entries.clue: Somersault and drop off backwards, tits beginning to get pert (8)

indicatorNotes.backwards: the word for drop off is written backwards
indicatorNotes.beginning: only the first letter of tits

blocks.note: to nap is to drop off to sleep; reversed to PAN

annotation.surface: A saucy picture of gymnastics leaving a woman's breasts perky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pert' in the surface describes breasts; as the definition it means cheeky, as in a pert reply.
annotation.definitionFit: Pert means cheeky and lacking respect, which is what flippant means.

entries.clue: Lying for Republicans in Alabama, say (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the Republican letter goes inside the word for a US state

blocks.note: Alabama is an example of a US state; it opens after ST

annotation.surface: A political jibe that Alabama Republicans are always lying.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lying' says dishonest in the surface; the answer is the other sense, lying face down.
annotation.definitionFit: Prostrate means lying flat, face downward.

entries.clue: On-screen activity? Bastard cheek! (4)

blocks.note: B = bastard, the euphemism in 'you little b'

annotation.surface: Someone watching the telly is outraged at the cheek of what is shown.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' looks like part of the face but is insolence, as in 'don't give me any lip'.
annotation.definitionFit: A blip is a spot of light on a radar screen showing an object.

entries.clue: Is beset by 'testicle twitch' – furious, having gone so (9)

indicatorNotes.beset by: IS is surrounded by the testicle and the twitch

blocks.note: used as it is, between the other two

annotation.surface: Someone with a twitch in a delicate place flies into a rage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Having gone so' completes the definition: someone furious has gone ballistic.
annotation.definitionFit: To go ballistic is to fly into a fury, so someone furious has gone ballistic.

entries.clue: Labour leader fared badly in hot temperature – which he strongly discourages (4,4)

indicatorNotes.in: the jumbled letters go inside H and T

blocks.note: L, Labour's first letter, with FARED, all rearranged

annotation.surface: A Labour leader did poorly in a heatwave and wants to discourage others from doing the same.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue's end: the Labour leader, Keir Starmer, discourages the hard left of his party. 'Hot temperature' splits into H and T, which wrap the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: The hard left is the radical wing of the Labour Party that its current leader works to sideline.

entries.clue: (& 25ac.) Maybe David Cameron's attempt to hide nothing look (4)

indicatorNotes.to hide: TRY hides the nothing inside it

blocks.note: a try is an attempt; it opens after T
to peer is to look closely

annotation.surface: A sneer at David Cameron's efforts to hide the fact that he has nothing to show.
annotation.walkthrough: David Cameron, a Conservative (Tory) prime minister, was later made Lord Cameron, a peer in the House of Lords. 'Cameron's' is 'Cameron has'. The answer runs on into 25 across.
annotation.definitionFit: Cameron sits in the House of Lords as a Conservative, so he is a Tory peer.

entries.clue: 'Road to nowhere' suitably clued as 'Conservative leader' (3-2-3)

indicatorNotes.suitably: the letters are rearranged to suit, into a fitting order
indicatorNotes.leader: only the first letter of Conservative

annotation.surface: A political wisecrack that 'road to nowhere' is a fair description of the Conservative leader.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a comment about crossword writing; in fact 'clued as C' is the raw material, rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A cul-de-sac is a dead-end road, a road that leads nowhere.

entries.clue: Be smarter than to publicly declare Oscar Wilde gay? (6)

blocks.note: to out someone is to publicly declare them gay
Oscar Wilde, the playwright, was a famous wit
completes the sense of 'publicly declare': to out someone is to declare them gay

annotation.surface: Exposing Oscar Wilde as gay is a way of getting one over on him.
annotation.walkthrough: Wilde was jailed for homosexuality, so outing him fits the surface; the setter wants only his fame as a wit.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to outwit someone is to get the better of them by being cleverer.

entries.clue: see 6dn.
Fan of CIA in terrible trouble (10)

indicatorNotes.terrible: 'of CIA in' is in a terrible state, so rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone who admires the CIA is in deep trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like it joins the definition to the rest; it is part of the fodder, and so is 'in'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym borrowed from Spanish, where an aficionado was a keen follower of bullfighting.

entries.clue: Is getting drowned in drink one way to form a union? (5)

annotation.definition: one way to form a union

indicatorNotes.getting drowned in: something drowned in drink is submerged inside it, so IS goes inside ALE

blocks.note: ale = drink; it opens after A

annotation.surface: A cynical question: is getting drunk the way to bring people together?
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is loose on purpose: couples walk down the aisle to marry, so the aisle is one route to that union.
annotation.definitionFit: Walking down the aisle is the way into a church wedding, a marriage union.

entries.clue: Le Pen wants agreement initially for European head to overturn country (5)

indicatorNotes.for: A goes in for, replacing, the E
indicatorNotes.head: the first letter of European
indicatorNotes.to overturn: the result is turned over, read upward

first letter of European, the letter replaced

annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Nepal, the Himalayan state between India and China, is one example of a country.

entries.clue: Top Labour and intensely remorseful Tory leaders keeping quiet (10)

indicatorNotes.leaders: the first letters of intensely, remorseful, Tory
indicatorNotes.keeping: those letters keep SH with them

annotation.walkthrough: 'Top Labour' looks like the Labour Party's chief; 'Top' is the garment and 'Labour' is hard work.
